# dtcloud_network (Resource)

Manages a network and, when IPAM is enabled, the subnet inside it.

One resource covers both because the API does not manage them apart: a single call creates the
network and its subnet, and the details endpoint reports them together.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A network with IPAM on: the provider also manages the subnet inside it.
resource "dtcloud_network" "app" {
  name         = "app-net"
  ipam_enabled = true
  cidr         = "10.20.0.0/24"

  gateway_ip      = "10.20.0.1"
  enable_dhcp     = true
  dns_nameservers = ["8.8.8.8", "8.8.4.4"]
}

# With IPAM off there is no subnet, and addresses are managed outside Terraform.
resource "dtcloud_network" "flat" {
  name         = "flat-net"
  ipam_enabled = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the network. Can be changed in place.

### Optional

- `allocation_pools` (Block List) Address ranges the subnet allocates from. The platform picks a sensible default when omitted. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--allocation_pools))
- `cidr` (String) IPv4 range for the subnet, e.g. 10.0.0.0/24. Required when ipam_enabled is true, and rejected when it is false. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `dns_nameservers` (List of String) DNS servers advertised to instances on this network.
- `enable_dhcp` (Boolean) Whether the subnet hands out addresses over DHCP.
- `gateway_ip` (String) Gateway address. The platform picks the first usable address when omitted.
- `ipam_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the platform manages addressing on this network. With it on, a subnet is created from `cidr` and port security is enabled. With it off there is no subnet at all: no CIDR, no gateway, no DHCP. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `ip_version` (Number) IP version of the subnet. The API creates IPv4 only.
- `network_type` (String) Virtual or Physical, as reported by the platform.
- `subnet_id` (String) ID of the subnet, empty when ipam_enabled is false.

<a id="nestedblock--allocation_pools"></a>
### Nested Schema for `allocation_pools`

Required:

- `end` (String) Last address in the range.
- `start` (String) First address in the range.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

~> **`ipam_enabled` is one flag doing two jobs.** It becomes the network's port security setting,
and it decides whether a subnet exists at all. With it off there is no subnet, so `cidr`,
`gateway_ip`, `dns_nameservers`, `allocation_pools` and `enable_dhcp = false` have nothing to apply
to, and setting any of them is refused at plan time.

* **What changes in place.** `name`, and the subnet's `gateway_ip`, `enable_dhcp`,
  `dns_nameservers` and `allocation_pools`. `ipam_enabled` and `cidr` force a new network: neither
  the subnet's address range nor its existence can be changed afterwards.
* **Subnet edits send the complete set.** The subnet endpoint requires `enable_dhcp`,
  `dns_nameservers` and `allocation_pools` together, so changing one of them sends all four subnet
  settings, `gateway_ip` included. A change made outside Terraform to one of them is overwritten the
  next time any of them changes here.
* **`ip_version` is not an argument.** The API creates IPv4 subnets whatever the request asks for,
  so the version is only reported back.
* **Creating and deleting are asynchronous.** A network has no status to poll, so the provider waits
  until it reads back, or stops resolving.

## Timeouts

`create` defaults to 15 minutes, `update` to 10 minutes and `delete` to 15 minutes. Override them
with a `timeouts` block:

```terraform
resource "dtcloud_network" "app" {
  # ...

  timeouts {
    create = "30m"
  }
}
```

## Import

```shell
terraform import dtcloud_network.app 3d2b9c88-4a71-4e5f-b0c2-9e8a1d7f4c33
```

Everything is read back, the subnet settings included, so a plan straight after an import is empty
when the configuration matches the network.
